notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 87-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.5, creatinine 0.7-0.75, hemoglobin 11.2-12.9, platelets 294-300, sodium 139, wbc 7.9-8.1; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 69-73, map 89-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 119-122, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.72-0.75, hemoglobin 10.3-11, platelets 297-302, sodium 139, wbc 7.9-8.4; vitals dbp 74-78, heart_rate 70-74, map 88-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 117-123, spo2 97-99, temp 36.8-37
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 87-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
